correctness.rationale: The proof classifies all possible closed factors into 0/1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 runs. The decisive five-run classification is: a mixed-symbol border exists exactly when the two intervening one-runs have equal length and both endpoint zero lengths fit in the middle zero-run; otherwise a purely zero border closes a factor exactly when the endpoint zero lengths are equal and exceed the middle run. Disjoint classes and one overlap subtraction give the formula. The upper bound follows from n >= 3(x+y)/2 + 2z, xy <= (x+y)^2/4 and an explicit lower construction at n=8k, extended monotonically to all n. A separate direct substring/border-occurrence checker confirms 3285 five-run exponent vectors and the recorded small-length maxima. It does not replace the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact number of closed factors (complete first returns) is a natural, established combinatorial and string-algorithmic invariant. Fixed-run restriction is motivated by the bitonic CR-poor characterization and the four-run quadratic construction, rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. The parameter-complete five-run census reveals a structural correction when the two interior runs coincide and proves a sharp 1/8 quadratic leading coefficient for the complete natural class. This is not a textbook substitution, finite table, or merely a small numerical gain. It does not claim the global extremal bound.
